featIpDesc: Point it at a host you already run. Reachable ports, service versions, matching CVEs by severity. Outside-in only. No login to the box, no agent for this step. You see what the internet can see before an auditor does.
featDomainDesc: One snapshot: DNS, TLS and expiry, security headers, detected stack. Catch a forgotten subdomain or a cert about to die. Posture, not a booking-flow test.
featMobileDesc: Upload the APK, AAB, or IPA you ship to guests or staff. Risky permissions, exported components, and secrets in the binary get flagged before the build hits a store.
featAttachDesc: A Friday nmap is a memory. A schedule is a control. Put the target on an interval, diff every run, and a new open port shows up as a change instead of a surprise.
featWorkspaceDesc: NOC, sysadmin, and the property contact read the same trail. No PDF ping-pong. Roles and invites per org. Credits stay on each login, not in a shared pot.
featAssetsDesc: Name the IP, domain, or app the way the team already says it, so a ticket reads "front-desk PMS" not a raw address. Each plan has a hard cap. The list stays real.
featGuardDesc: One wazuh-agent per VM. Inventory of what is installed and running, plus critical alerts. Thin on purpose. Not a SIEM console. Not a dashboard to babysit.
featUptimeDesc: Probe a URL or TCP port from outside. Record when it stops answering. Reachability only. It does not read CVEs and it is not an SLA on your rack or upstream.
featCreditsDesc: Each scan draws from the balance on your account. A heavy audit month costs more than a quiet one. Nothing is metered behind your back. Prices are not on this page.

heroSub: The rack, the VPS, and the property uplink are already invoiced. Sinexis attaches to that: scheduled outside-in scans of your IPs, domains, and mobile builds, then one thin agent on the VM for inventory and critical alerts. Periodic scan is not 24/7 SIEM. Host Protect reads disk through a helper on the machine and reports nothing when it finds nothing. One wazuh-agent per host. Not a human pentest.

notFoundBody: That URL is not a Sinexis page. Go home, or sign in for the workspace, scans, and Guard hosts.
stepScanDesc: Start with one IP, domain, or mobile build you own. The run is outside-in. You get an HTML report you can hand to a client or an auditor.
stepAttachDesc: Set the interval to match how often the infra changes. Each run diffs against the last, so you review the delta, not the whole report again.
stepWorkspaceDesc: Invite the team into one org. Assets get real names. History stays in one place. Tonight's shift sees what the last scan found.
stepGuardDesc: Install one wazuh-agent on the VM. It reports installed packages and running services, then raises critical alerts. That closes the loop: Scan → Attach → Workspace → Guard.
siemNote: SIEM log search and Cases (incident tickets in our Postgres, not a Wazuh plugin) sit behind an ops flag and are not sold as a live feature here. Host WAF runs in your nginx on your server, never on the Sinexis edge.
faqAuthQ: Do I need permission to scan?
faqAuthA: Yes. Scan only hosts, domains, and apps you own or are authorized in writing to test. Managing a property or a client rack still needs that authorization before the first run. Unauthorized scanning is not allowed.
faqPentestA: No. Automated outside-in scanning on a schedule. Exposed services, weak TLS, missing headers, known CVEs. Not business logic, not chained abuse, not your booking flow. If a contract needs a manual pentest, keep it. Use this to stay clean between engagements.
faqDataA: Findings and reports stay in your workspace, visible to members you invite. Retention is in the privacy policy. Do not upload credentials or secrets you are not allowed to store off your own systems.
faqGuardQ: Guard vs SIEM vs Host Protect?
faqGuardA: Guard is the thin agent view: inventory plus critical alerts, no log-hunting UI. SIEM is log search plus Cases (incident tickets in our Postgres), off by default, not sold live here. Host Protect is a helper on the VM that reads web directories for on-box malware. Missing helper or unreachable path: we say so and return no hits. We do not invent malware to fill a screen.
faqAgentA: No. One wazuh-agent per machine, enrolled once to your org. Host Protect is a helper script on that same machine, not a second daemon.
